Same-term direction is permitted (earlier-to-same term) and the reverse reading is not supported, since sentence copying does not specifically enable word spacing. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Reading skills from the same framework, but at different terms: the second ('Understands that print communicates meaning. Knows words can represent own name, names of people, places and things') sits under Grade R TERM 2, Sub-strand 'Emergent reading', while the first ('Begins to recognise that words are made up of sounds such as the beginning letter/s of their names') sits under Grade R TERM 4, Sub-strand 'Phonological/Phonemic Awareness'. The Term 2 statement establishes the concept of a word in print and that a word can represent the learner's own name (LC tags: print awareness, words, names); the Term 4 statement extends this from whole-word/print meaning to the internal sound structure of those same words, using the beginning letter/s of the child's name (LC tags: beginning sounds, names, phonemic awareness). That is a substantive deepening from word-as-unit print awareness to sound-within-word awareness anchored on the same familiar name content, so proficiency with the Term 2 understanding supports success with the Term 4 phonemic skill. Direction second_to_first keeps the within-grade order earlier Term 2 to later Term 4, which is permitted. Shared Grade R ancestry and overlapping tokens ('words', 'names') alone were not treated as sufficient; the judgment rests on the pair-specific conceptual progression. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and both carry upstream merge/audit context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.
